boundary_conditions: Do not open with industry background before naming the object.
features.clause_structure: single main clause
features.modality: declarative
original_instantiations: This paper addresses the problem of scheduling the maximum number of rafting trips along the Big Long River.
features.quantitative_role: none
replaceable_slots: This paper addresses the problem of {object}
features.tense: present
features.voice: first person plural then impersonal

units.function: Open by naming the decision object and its scale before any method.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open with industry background before naming the object.
reusable_elements: This paper addresses the problem of {object}
units.reusable_pattern: object -> scale
units.source_excerpt: This paper addresses the problem of scheduling the maximum number of rafting trips along the Big Long River.

boundary_conditions: Do not present a single-objective optimum when the problem has competing criteria.
features.clause_structure: main clause plus while-clause
features.modality: descriptive
original_instantiations: An optimal schedule for this problem would minimize the number of crossovers while maximizing the percentage of campsites used and matching a target distribution of trip lengths.
features.quantitative_role: three criteria
replaceable_slots: An optimal {object} would {criterion one} while {criterion two} and {criterion three}
features.tense: conditional
features.voice: impersonal

units.function: Define the objective as a three-way trade-off rather than a single maximum.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a single-objective optimum when the problem has competing criteria.
reusable_elements: An optimal {object} would {criterion one} while {criterion two} and {criterion three}
units.reusable_pattern: objective -> criterion one -> criterion two -> criterion three
units.source_excerpt: An optimal schedule for this problem would minimize the number of crossovers while maximizing the percentage of campsites used and matching a target distribution of trip lengths.

boundary_conditions: Do not leave the number of models implicit when the body compares them.
features.clause_structure: one short clause
features.modality: declarative
original_instantiations: Three main models are proposed for this problem.
features.quantitative_role: cardinal
replaceable_slots: {n} main models are proposed for this problem
features.tense: present
features.voice: impersonal

units.function: Announce how many models follow so the reader can allocate attention.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the number of models implicit when the body compares them.
reusable_elements: {n} main models are proposed for this problem
units.reusable_pattern: count -> handoff
units.source_excerpt: Three main models are proposed for this problem.

boundary_conditions: Do not describe a model by its objective alone; name what one iteration does.
features.clause_structure: main clause plus by-clause
features.modality: procedural
original_instantiations: The Priority Model iteratively generates a schedule by scheduling trip locations daily and allows for crossovers.
features.quantitative_role: none
replaceable_slots: The {name} Model iteratively {operation} by {detail} and allows for {relaxation}
features.tense: present
features.voice: impersonal

units.function: Explain the first model through the operation it repeats.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe a model by its objective alone; name what one iteration does.
reusable_elements: The {name} Model iteratively {operation} by {detail} and allows for {relaxation}
units.reusable_pattern: model name -> iteration -> operation -> permission
units.source_excerpt: The Priority Model iteratively generates a schedule by scheduling trip locations daily and allows for crossovers.

boundary_conditions: Do not omit the stopping condition of a repair loop.
features.clause_structure: two coordinated stages
features.modality: procedural
original_instantiations: The Density Perturbation Model places all trips at their optimal campsites and then iteratively perturbs this structure until no trips are in conflict.
features.quantitative_role: none
replaceable_slots: The {name} Model places ... and then iteratively perturbs ... until {condition}
features.tense: present
features.voice: impersonal

units.function: Explain the second model as construct-then-repair with a stopping rule.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the stopping condition of a repair loop.
reusable_elements: The {name} Model places ... and then iteratively perturbs ... until {condition}
units.reusable_pattern: model name -> construction -> repair -> stopping rule
units.source_excerpt: The Density Perturbation Model places all trips at their optimal campsites and then iteratively perturbs this structure until no trips are in conflict.

boundary_conditions: Do not present a greedy heuristic as if it were exact.
features.clause_structure: main clause plus participial phrase
features.modality: descriptive
original_instantiations: The Bone Growth Model solves for a schedule with no crossovers globally using a heuristic greedy algorithm that builds off an initial input sequence of trips.
features.quantitative_role: none
replaceable_slots: The {name} Model solves for {guarantee} using a heuristic ... that builds off {seed}
features.tense: present
features.voice: impersonal

units.function: Explain the third model by the guarantee it gives and where the algorithm comes from.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a greedy heuristic as if it were exact.
reusable_elements: The {name} Model solves for {guarantee} using a heuristic ... that builds off {seed}
